units.function: Unit tests for a per-Run cap on Agent comments and updates that affect issues other than the Run source issue.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> cross-issue influence service -> transaction-shaped in-memory database stub modeling Run lock, activity count and activity inserts; no real route, issue authorization or PostgreSQL.
units.keyDataModels: Company/Agent/Run/source issue/target issue, responsibleUserId on the Run, influence kind, accepted/rejected activity actions, fixed cap/mode/enforcement timestamp and structured error details.
units.lifecycle: Agent requests cross-issue write -> service validates locked Run context -> counts prior influence activity -> evaluates rollout/cap -> records accepted or rejected receipt -> caller may proceed or receive 429-style denial.
units.testAssessment: All 9 unit tests passed. They strongly cover boundary arithmetic and fail-closed Run binding under a stub, but omit terminal Runs, active accountable human, target authorization, risk/effect classes, idempotency, business-mutation atomicity and audit retention manipulation. Real concurrency is delegated to a separate skipped suite.
units.designRationale: Contain unbounded task drift by letting Agents make a limited number of visible cross-task effects per heartbeat while first observing behavior in a timed log-only rollout.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs runtime-enforced work containment so an Agent cannot broaden its goal, data or tool effects beyond the exact authorized Work/Responsibility contract without a risk-matched human decision.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the persisted Run binding, fail-closed context validation, structured denial and durable accepted/rejected receipt. Replace the universal count with effect-class capability budgets and exact target/data/tool/action digests; bind an active accountable human and responsibility contract, require idempotency, and atomically couple authorization consumption, business effect and evidence/outbox state.
units.responsibilityConflict: A responsibleUserId exists on the Run but is not validated or included in the decision contract. Twenty cross-work effects are allowed regardless of human authority, effect risk or approval; a numeric behavioral limit is not a responsibility chain.
evidence: 2026-08-19 focused Vitest: 9/9 passed in sandboxed and approved unsandboxed runs
units.securityFindings: HIGH authorization-model gap: fixed count replaces effect/risk/capability authorization and does not validate the accountable human. HIGH integrity gap: activity log doubles as mutable enforcement counter without tested retention protection or event idempotency. HIGH atomicity gap: no test proves counter consumption and the eventual issue mutation commit or roll back together. Missing cases include terminal/cancelled Run, other-tenant target, duplicate retry, stale approval, parallel distinct targets, same-issue high-risk effects, direct activity inserts and stable reset semantics.

units.function: Embedded-PostgreSQL concurrency test intended to prove exactly one of the twentieth and twenty-first simultaneous cross-issue writes is allowed.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> real cross-issue service -> real Paperclip database schema and embedded PostgreSQL when supported; no route, authorization or actual issue mutation.
units.keyDataModels: Company, Agent, running heartbeat Run, responsible human id and accepted/rejected activity-log counter rows.
units.lifecycle: Seed 19 accepted receipts -> race two transactions against one Run -> expect serialized counts 20/21 -> persist one accepted and one rejected receipt.
units.testAssessment: The assertion targets the correct concurrency property, but the suite skipped in both sandboxed and approved unsandboxed executions because embedded PostgreSQL support was unavailable. It therefore supplies design intent rather than verified runtime evidence here, and omits deadlock/retry/rollback/crash behavior.
units.designRationale: Use database locking and durable activity rows so horizontal server concurrency cannot overrun the cross-issue effect cap.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs durable, horizontally safe consumption of capability/approval budgets and exactly-once evidence across local and managed deployment profiles.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the real-database race test shape into mandatory PostgreSQL and local-database compatibility tests for a generic authorization-consumption ledger. Extend it to idempotency, retry, rollback, outbox publication, crash recovery and policy-version/approval-digest binding before accepting the design.
units.responsibilityConflict: Serialization protects a counter, not the accountable-human decision or final business effect. The fixture's responsibleUserId is passive metadata and the source/target Work has no responsibility contract.
evidence: 2026-08-19 focused Vitest in sandbox and approved unsandboxed modes: 1/1 PostgreSQL test skipped
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL verification gap for the claimed concurrency invariant: the only real-database test did not execute. HIGH atomicity gap: it stops at counter receipts and never races or rolls back the protected business mutation. Missing cases include lock timeout/deadlock, transaction retry, process crash, duplicate idempotency key, activity retention/deletion, terminal Run and responsibility/approval revocation during contention.
